items.title: Chronic stress activates the HPA axis
items.claim: The hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA) axis produces cortisol in response to stress. What does chronic activation cause?

options.text: Sustained elevation of cortisol is associated with immune suppression, abdominal fat deposition, hippocampal atrophy, and increased cardiovascular risk — moving stress from a psychological to a physiological problem
Cortisol stops being produced under chronic stress

items.reveal:
Hans Selye described the General Adaptation Syndrome (alarm, resistance, exhaustion) in 1936. Bruce McEwen's concept of 'allostatic load' (1998) extends this: the wear-and-tear of repeated stress responses contributes to chronic disease.

Whitehall studies (Marmot, 1967 onwards) linked low job control with worse health outcomes via stress pathways. The relationship between psychosocial stress and cardiovascular disease is robust across cohorts but causality is hard to isolate from confounders.
items.why: The mind-body distinction breaks down when looking at chronic stress. Psychological experience produces measurable biological change with health consequences.

items.title: The Health Belief Model predicts (some) preventive behaviours
items.claim: Rosenstock's 1974 Health Belief Model proposes that preventive behaviour depends on perceived susceptibility, severity, benefits and barriers. What's its empirical track record?

options.text: It predicts all health behaviours perfectly

Meta-analyses (Carpenter 2010) find modest predictive power: perceived barriers strongest, perceived benefits moderate, susceptibility and severity weaker. The model under-weights social and emotional factors
It only applies to dental hygiene

items.reveal:
Rosenstock developed the HBM from 1950s public health work on TB screening uptake. It has been applied to vaccination, screening, smoking cessation and COVID behaviours.

Competitors and extensions: Theory of Planned Behavior (Ajzen 1991, adds intention and perceived control); Transtheoretical Model (Prochaska 1979, stages of change). Behavioural economics (EAST framework: easy, attractive, social, timely) is the more recent UK policy framework.
items.why: Behaviour-change theories provide testable frameworks but rarely explain more than a fraction of variance. Combining them with structural interventions usually outperforms either alone.

items.title: Re-evaluating Stanford Prison
items.claim: Philip Zimbardo's 1971 Stanford Prison Experiment is often cited as proof that situations dictate behaviour. What did later archival work by Le Texier and others reveal?

options.text: Guards received explicit coaching, undermining the 'natural' interpretation
No participant played the guard role

items.reveal_title: Guards were coached, not spontaneously behaving
items.reveal:
Le Texier's 2018 archival analysis and a 2019 American Psychologist article showed guards received briefings encouraging tough behaviour.

The BBC Prison Study (Reicher & Haslam, 2006) produced very different dynamics under similar setup.
items.why: Replication and archival work reshape how landmark findings are interpreted.
